paper_metadata.title: Multiobjective variational quantum optimization for constrained problems: an application to Cash Management

summary: The paper introduces MOVCO, a multi‑objective genetic‑algorithm optimizer for variational quantum algorithms, and evaluates it on Cash Management optimization instances with up to 16 qubits (2 ATMs over 4 days) and up to 308 binary variables using a product‑state ansatz. Across 120 simulated instances with 8192 measurement shots per circuit, MOVCO‑VQE achieves higher constraint‑satisfaction rates and better approximation ratios than penalty‑based VQE, often reaching feasible solutions within ~200 generations. All results are obtained via noiseless classical simulation rather than quantum hardware.

experiments.description: MOVCO-VQE on randomly generated Cash Management Problem instances using a one-layer hardware-efficient VQE ansatz and NSGA-II multiobjective classical optimization.

algorithm.variant: MOVCO-VQE (Multi-Objective Variational Constrained Optimizer with VQE)
algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient ansatz with parameterized single-qubit Ry rotations and nearest-neighbor CZ entangling gates
algorithm.optimizer: NSGA-II (binary tournament selection, simulated binary crossover, polynomial mutation)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: fixed number of generations / evaluations; results reported up to 400 generations and 8192 shots per evaluation
algorithm.parameter_initialization: parameters initialized around pi/4 with small random perturbations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: binary/spin encoding of discretized cash levels; V = 2CD binary variables for C cash points and D days
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize transaction cost C(z) while maximizing constraint satisfaction P(theta) via a two-objective Pareto optimization; restricted energy E(theta) computed only over feasible samples
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: feasibility filter via multiobjective optimization (maximize percentage of satisfied constraints and minimize restricted energy); no penalty terms in MOVCO
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Cash Management Hamiltonian expressed in Pauli-Z operators (Eq. 16)

problem_instance.description: Cash Management Problem instances with 2 cash points over 2, 3, and 4 days

dataset_specification.description: cash-point delivery costs drawn from discrete uniform [1,4], first-day cost doubled; initial predictions drawn from discrete uniform [-2,5]; last-day total cash limit v = C; max daily transactions l = 1 if C=2 else floor(C/2)

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 120 random instances; classical simulation; 8192 sampled bitstrings per circuit evaluation; performance tracked over generations

hardware.framework: pymoo 0.5.0 for NSGA-II optimization; quantum circuits simulated classically (noise‑free) using HPC resources

noise_model.noise_type: noise-free classical simulation of quantum circuit

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: random CMP instance generation; discretization of cash levels; mapping to spin variables
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Pareto-front selection; approximation ratio and constraint-satisfaction metrics computed from sampled bitstrings

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: two-stage behavior: first increase constraint satisfaction, then minimize restricted energy

speedup_claims.caveats: No quantum advantage or speedup claim is made; the paper reports empirical performance only.

limiting_factors: No comparison with best classical optimization algorithms for CMP

experiments.description: Large‑scale benchmark using a fully separable product‑state ansatz to compare MOVCO‑VQE and VQE with penalties on larger Cash Management instances.

algorithm.variant: MOVCO‑VQE vs penalized VQE with product‑state ansatz
algorithm.ansatz: fully separable product state |ψ(θ)⟩ = ∏n (cos θn |0⟩ + sin θn |1⟩)
algorithm.optimizer: MOVCO: NSGA‑II; baseline: VQE with penalties using SPSA or genetic algorithm

key_results: Problem sizes scaled to 10–22 cash points over 7 days corresponding to up to V = 308 binary variables/qubits.
MOVCO consistently achieved better constraint satisfaction and lower transaction cost than penalty‑based VQE across evaluation budgets up to ~10,000 circuit evaluations.
Improvement observed for 100% of tested instances at 10,000 evaluations (Fig.9).

experiments.description: Appendix C experiment comparing MOVCO‑VQE with a single‑objective genetic algorithm optimizer applied to penalized VQE.

algorithm.variant: MOVCO‑VQE vs penalized VQE optimized with a genetic algorithm
algorithm.ansatz: same one‑layer hardware‑efficient ansatz with Ry rotations and CZ entangling gates
algorithm.optimizer: MOVCO: NSGA‑II multiobjective GA; baseline: single‑objective GA minimizing penalized Hamiltonian

key_results: MOVCO achieved higher feasibility rates and lower dispersion of approximation ratios across 120 CMP instances.
Results similar to SPSA baseline comparison, confirming advantage arises from the multiobjective formulation rather than the optimizer alone (Appendix C, Fig.11).
